analysis:
All three changed files are test-only: DoctorOperatorDiagnosisTests.swift (new coordinatorTraffic test, head lines 95-137), StatusCommandRunTests.swift (new trafficVerdict and heldProviderHasNoTrafficVerdict tests, head lines 121-207) and the added ServingReadinessTests.swift (ServingReadiness verdict tests and UnauthorizedConnectionRecoveryTests). No production code is in this batch, so no auth, crypto, routing or trust-boundary behavior changes here.

The tests encode intended operator-diagnostic behavior around TB-011, T-052, T-053, T-057, A-016 and A-018. A legacy or App Attest authorized path is reported as 'eligible' only from the coordinator-supplied authorization object (path app_attest, unexpired, or legacy). Local state or the shadow evidence alone is not treated as permission, which is consistent with T-052. An expired lease, path none, an untrusted status or a disconnect is reported as blocked. A coordinator that sends no authorization object and gives only self_signed trust yields no verdict, so the tests do not overclaim serving. An add-on hold suppresses the traffic verdict (TB-012/T-059), but a disconnect still reports blocked.

The tests use synthetic values such as 'session', 'machine-1' and 'attestation-key', with no real secrets or identifiers. Child-process sandboxes use a stub coordinator at coordinator.invalid.

For the next pass: the production implementations (ServingReadiness, UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery, Status and Doctor wiring, and the DaemonState.coordinatorConnection persistence) are not in this batch. Check there that diagnostic 'eligible' output is advisory only and that the reconnect recovery policy (threshold, backoff, idle-only) cannot be abused to bypass App Attest or MDM gating. These tests do not prove those properties.
